chunks.title: Negative-money patterns: observations, not a refund classification
chunks.text: ## Negative-money patterns: observations, not a refund classification The raw negative-money flag covers 2,853,594 records, of which 2,853,180 are operational. Flex Fare accounts for 2,047,090 raw negative-money records (71.74% of the flag). Of those, 1,879,872 have a negative fare_amount but nonnegative total_amount. It is not unmet demand, available taxis, vehicle rebalancing needs or proof of causation. The displayed comparison selects ten NYC zones with the largest positive differences and ten with the largest negative differences. Whole-population pickup and drop-off sums each reconcile to 48,157,684, including unknown/off-city endpoints. A NYC-only subtotal need not balance because trips can cross its boundary. chunks.text: ## JFK-to-JFK records There are 107,448 operational records whose pickup and drop-off both have zone ID 132. chunks.title: Interactive aggregation contract
chunks.text: ## Interactive aggregation contract The explorer uses a calendar-complete 365-date × 262-observed-pickup-ID snapshot (95,630 rows). Missing date/zone combinations contain zero additive activity; this prevents sparse zones from losing zero-trip days. Date, pickup borough and zone filters apply to all explorer charts and cards. Counts and sums are additive. Mean fare = SUM(eligible fare_amount)/SUM(fare_n); mean total charge uses the same fare_n. Average daily trips = SUM(trips)/COUNTD(selected pickup_date). No average of zone means or group medians is used. Annual/historical dashboards remain explicitly fixed summaries, and the explorer contains no filtered median because exact medians cannot be reconstructed from its compact daily aggregates.

chunks.title: Measures and correct aggregation
chunks.text: ## Measures and correct aggregation `trips` is the operational count. `fare_n` counts operational and fare-eligible records; `distance_n` counts operational records with distance between 0 and 100 miles inclusive. `duration_sum_min` covers all operational trips. Fare and charge sums use only fare-eligible records. `distance_sum_mi` uses valid-distance records. Card-tip sums/counts apply to fare-eligible card records with a recorded tip; these do not measure cash tips. CBD-fee sums/counts cover fare-eligible records with a recorded CBD fee. Negative fees are not silently dropped when the trip otherwise passes fare eligibility. Combined means must divide combined sums by combined denominators: fare sum/fare_n; charge sum/fare_n; duration sum/trips; distance sum/distance_n; card tip sum/card_tip_n; CBD fee sum/cbd_fee_n. Missing eligible values remain null; empty denominators produce no mean. Stored median_duration_min, p90_duration_min and median_fare_usd are exact only for their stored group. Never average them to calculate a larger group's percentile.

chunks.title: What is the busiest pickup hour? Peak hourly trips and demand
chunks.text:
For 2025 operational trips, the busiest pickup hour is 18:00-18:59. It contains 3,431,144 annual pickups, 9,400 average daily pickups and 7.12% of operational trips. These are completed-record counts, not unmet demand.
Evidence: data/hourly_dashboard_2025.csv

chunks.title: When do recorded meter fare totals peak?
chunks.text:
Recorded meter-fare totals peak at 17:00 in 2025. Operational pickup counts peak at 18:00. The fare series uses fare-eligible records; the pickup series uses all operational records. No causal explanation for the difference is established.
Evidence: data/hourly_dashboard_2025.csv

chunks.title: How many total operational trips and average daily trips are there?
chunks.text:
The 2025 operational population is 48,157,684 trips. Average daily operational activity is 131,939 trips, using all 365 calendar dates. The total is not the raw published count.
Evidence: data/annual_2025.csv

chunks.title: Why were 564,918 records excluded? What is the cleaning funnel?
chunks.text:
Published 2025 records: 48,722,602. Operational trips: 48,157,684. Fare-eligible records: 44,727,165. Operational exclusions total 564,918: 214 pickups outside source month, 546,304 nonpositive durations and 18,400 durations over 180 minutes, in disjoint priority order. Missing timestamps add zero exclusions.
Evidence: data/cleaning_funnel.csv; data/cleaning_waterfall.csv

chunks.title: Why are 48.16 million operational trips different from 44.73 million fare eligible records?
chunks.text:
The 48,157,684 operational trips include records that fail fare eligibility. A further 3,430,519 records are excluded from fare analysis: 2,853,180 negative fare/charge records, then 577,339 disputed payments with nonnegative money. The remaining 44,727,165 are fare eligible. Payment and money must be nonmissing; money nonnegative; payment not 4 or 6.
Evidence: data/cleaning_waterfall.csv

chunks.title: What does payment code 0 mean? Is it unspecified or unknown?
chunks.text:
The TLC yellow taxi dictionary dated 18 March 2025 defines payment code 0 as Flex Fare. It is not missing or unspecified payment. Flex Fare has 11,609,242 operational trips (24.11%) and 9,562,369 eligible fare records. Code 5 Unknown contains only 2 operational records.
Evidence: data/payment_diagnostics.csv; QUALITY_INVESTIGATION.md

chunks.title: Are negative fares refunds? What did the money investigation find?
chunks.text:
Negative money is not established to represent refunds. Flex Fare contains 2,047,090 raw negative-money records. Of these, 1,879,872 have negative fare and nonnegative charge. The most frequent such fare value is -4.75 (1,048,380 raw records). The source dictionary does not explain the cause.
Evidence: data/payment_diagnostics.csv; data/negative_money_patterns.csv; data/flex_negative_fare_values.csv

chunks.title: Does a matching positive counterpart prove refunds or duplicates?
chunks.text:
Of 968,516 operational records with both money values negative, 712,945 have at least one matching positive counterpart: timestamps, zone IDs and distance match and fare/charge have opposite signs and equal magnitudes. This is an existence test, not a one-to-one transaction match. It proves neither refunds nor duplication. No deduplication was applied.
Evidence: data/negative_counterpart_check.csv; QUALITY_INVESTIGATION.md

chunks.title: Why are there JFK to JFK trips? What are the same-zone caveats?
chunks.text:
PU132/DO132 means both endpoints share the JFK taxi zone, not identical GPS positions. There are 107,448 operational records; 43,026 (40.04%) have zero recorded distance. Median duration is 0.3 minutes; p90 12.2 minutes. The cause and transaction validity are not established.
Evidence: data/jfk_within_zone_diagnostics.csv

chunks.title: Which NYC zone has more drop-offs than pickups? Largest net arrivals
chunks.text:
East Harlem South has the largest positive annual NYC balance: 550,093 drop-offs minus 355,891 pickups = +194,202. This is an observed endpoint difference, not a recommendation about taxi supply.
Evidence: data/zone_pickup_dropoff_2025.csv

chunks.title: Which NYC zone has more pickups than drop-offs? Largest net departures
chunks.text:
JFK Airport has the largest negative annual NYC balance: 453,087 drop-offs minus 2,047,254 pickups = -1,594,167. Balance is drop-offs minus pickups; negative means more pickups.
Evidence: data/zone_pickup_dropoff_2025.csv

chunks.title: How is pickup versus drop-off zone balance calculated?
chunks.text:
Zone balance = drop-offs minus pickups. Each of the same 48,157,684 operational records contributes one pickup and one drop-off. Positive means more arrivals; negative means more departures. Global endpoint totals reconcile; NYC subtotals need not because other endpoints can be off-city or unknown.
Evidence: data/zone_pickup_dropoff_2025.csv

chunks.title: How did January August 2026 change versus 2025? Historical volume decrease
chunks.text:
January-August 2026 has 29,703,355 published records versus 31,556,438 in January-August 2025, a -5.9% change. These are raw source-file counts, not cleaned operational trips. Neither period is annualized; no cause is established.
Evidence: data/historical_comparable.csv

chunks.title: Do you have every trip from previous years? What is the dataset coverage?
chunks.text:
Historical coverage is January 2009 through August 2026: 212 verified monthly source-file footers. Earlier trip records were not downloaded or cleaned. Detailed operational analysis uses all twelve 2025 trip files. The 2026 period is partial, January-August only.
Evidence: SCOPE.md; Analysis_Report.pdf

chunks.title: What are median trip duration and p90? Exact pooled statistics
chunks.text:
The 2025 operational median duration is 13.6 minutes and p90 is 32.8 minutes. Exact pooled SQL quantile_cont values are used. P90 is a percentile of recorded observations, not a guaranteed travel time. Monthly medians are not averaged into the annual median.
Evidence: data/annual_2025.csv; DATA_DICTIONARY.md

chunks.title: What are median recorded meter fare and total charge?
chunks.text:
For 44,727,165 eligible 2025 records, median meter fare is USD 14.49 and median recorded total charge is USD 22.13. Subtracting these medians does not produce the median surcharge. Monetary values are nominal USD.
Evidence: data/annual_2025.csv

chunks.title: What is average mean fare per trip and total charge?
chunks.text:
For 44,727,165 eligible 2025 records, mean recorded meter fare is USD 20.15 and mean recorded total charge is USD 28.95. Each mean divides the selected monetary sum by its eligible record count.
Evidence: data/annual_2025.csv

chunks.title: Is the 901.3 million fare total collected revenue, profit or earnings?
chunks.text:
The 2025 eligible recorded meter-fare sum is USD 901.3 million. It is a sum of recorded fare_amount values, not a measurement of collected revenue, driver earnings or profit. Cash tips are absent; costs and driver shifts are not supplied.
Evidence: data/annual_2025.csv; Analysis_Report.pdf

chunks.title: How are missing negative abnormal or zero distance records handled?
chunks.text:
Distance summaries use nonmissing reported meter miles from 0 to 100 inclusive. Zero distance is retained. Negative, missing and above-100-mile distance values affect distance metrics only, not otherwise eligible operational counts. The annual distance median is 1.85 miles before display rounding. Unknown zones remain in global activity.
Evidence: DATA_DICTIONARY.md; data/annual_2025.csv

chunks.title: How are trips by hour daily averages and weekday heatmap calculated?
chunks.text:
Annual trips in each pickup hour are divided by all 365 calendar days. Weekday hourly patterns divide by 261 weekdays; weekend patterns by 104 weekend dates. Weekday-hour heatmap cells divide by the number of that weekday: Wednesday 53, other weekdays 52 in 2025. Missing date-zone activity is represented by zero rows in the Explorer calendar.
Evidence: DATA_DICTIONARY.md; Analysis_Report.pdf

chunks.title: Can I average monthly medians or filter daily average and fares?
chunks.text:
Explorer date, pickup borough and taxi zone filters apply to seven views. Daily average = selected trips / distinct selected calendar dates, including zero-activity rows. Mean fare = selected eligible fare sum / selected fare-eligible count. Stored group medians cannot be averaged into filtered medians. The other dashboards are fixed full-year reference views.
Evidence: DATA_DICTIONARY.md; Analysis_Report.pdf

chunks.title: Can the data explain causes, predict future demand, driver profit or taxi rebalancing?
chunks.text:
No causal explanation, forecast, driver profit, utilization, unmet-demand estimate or optimal taxi allocation is established by this analysis. Completed trip records lack failed requests, passenger queues, vehicle availability, costs and driver-shift information. Negative-money meanings and short within-JFK records remain unresolved.
Evidence: Analysis_Report.pdf; QUALITY_INVESTIGATION.md

chunks.title: Metric and population guide
chunks.text: # Metric and population guide

chunks.title: Three populations
chunks.text:
## Three populations
Historical counts mean published source-file rows, before cleaning. Detailed 2025 operational trips require source-month-matched pickup, both timestamps and duration greater than zero and at most 180 minutes. Fare eligibility is an operational subset with nonmissing nonnegative fare/charge and payment not disputed or voided. Do not mix their denominators.

chunks.title: Monetary fields
chunks.text:
## Monetary fields
fare_amount is recorded meter fare; total_amount is the recorded total passenger charge. Cash tips are absent. Recorded sums do not establish collected revenue, profit or driver earnings. Means divide monetary sums by fare-eligible counts. Separate medians cannot be subtracted to obtain median surcharges.

chunks.title: Percentiles and distance
chunks.text:
## Percentiles and distance
SQL exact pooled quantile_cont calculates median and p90. Percentiles are not additive and stored group medians cannot be averaged. Distance metrics separately require reported distance from 0 through 100 miles inclusive. Zero distance remains eligible for distance and activity.

chunks.title: Endpoint and map geography
chunks.text:
## Endpoint and map geography
Net zone balance equals drop-offs minus pickups. Positive means more recorded arrivals and negative more recorded departures. Both endpoint counts use the same operational records. Cross-boundary and unknown endpoints can prevent NYC subtotals balancing. Tableau's density map weights 259 representative NYC zone points by pickups; these are approximate zone locations, not trip GPS.

chunks.title: Daily denominators
chunks.text:
## Daily denominators
Hourly daily activity uses all 365 calendar days in 2025, or 261 weekdays and 104 weekend days. Heatmap weekday counts use actual occurrences. Selected Explorer daily averages use all selected dates, including zero-activity date-zone combinations. Fare means use selected eligible counts.

Evidence: DATA_DICTIONARY.md, Analysis_Report.pdf pages 2-4, 6-8 and 10; retained SQL summary tables.

chunks.title: Questions the evidence cannot answer
chunks.text: # Questions the evidence cannot answer

chunks.title: Causes and predictions
chunks.text:
## Causes and predictions
The analysis is descriptive. It does not identify causes of the 2026 matching-period volume difference, explain every negative-money record, establish why pickup and fare-total peaks differ, or forecast future activity. No claims about weather, policy or market causes are established.

chunks.title: Financial and operational outcomes
chunks.text:
## Financial and operational outcomes
There is no operating-cost, driver-shift, taxi-availability, failed-request or passenger-queue evidence. Driver earnings, profit, utilization, unmet demand, business savings and optimal fleet allocation are not measured. Reported fares are recorded fields, not collected revenue. Cash tips are absent.

chunks.title: Transactions and short trips
chunks.text:
## Transactions and short trips
An opposite-money counterpart existence check is not a one-to-one refund or duplicate match. Same airport zone IDs do not establish identical GPS locations. Short and zero-distance within-JFK records require transaction or vendor context before their causes can be explained.

chunks.title: Coverage and source updates
chunks.text:
## Coverage and source updates
The source snapshot was checked 12 October 2026. Detailed trip analysis covers January-December 2025; historical raw footer counts cover January 2009-August 2026. Earlier trip-level fields and future or live data are outside this knowledge base. Raw flag counts overlap; do not sum them as exclusions.

Evidence: Analysis_Report.pdf pages 3-4 and 8-10; QUALITY_INVESTIGATION.md; SCOPE.md. This document states evidence boundaries, not new empirical findings.
